chapter: Left out of the jazz books; Tatum, Handy and family
title: Music in the film, a scene in 'Blazing Saddles', and the instruments he plays
summary: Other veterans did the Lady Sings the Blues music; Collins also played in a scene of Blazing Saddles with Basie and says he plays guitar, banjo, classical guitar and clarinet under protest.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: way, we did a lot of -- Sweets did a lot of music also, but they had quite a few of the guys, of the older guys. I think Cat Anderson was doing some of the music, Marshall Royal, Calendar Red Calendar, Oliver Nelson, Gil Askey Askey, to name a few. That was one of the music of the movies that I was in. I also did -- did you see "Blazing Saddles"?
No, not yet, are you in there?
Well, I was in Count's band then. Basie's band. We did one scene in this, and we all got a shot so you would have --
Was this Basie's regular band or --

Well, no, it was guys who had been with Basie, you know. Fellas who had said hello to him some time or other, you know. So any way, we did this shot in the desert, and we played April in Paris in the desert. It's another --
I understand it's a very funny scene (Inaudible)
Yeah, yeah. So they flew Basie in just for that one shot, and flew him right back, you know. So I want to go on record as saying that I do play guitar, and I have played guitar, banjo --
No, that's just about it. Just a banjo and guitar, and of course the other 12 string and you know a little bass guitar. But those -- I do that just for commercial you know --

Yeah, well I play classical guitar because I love classical guitar. So I do that. But as I say, I just want to go on record to say that I do play the string instrument, and I have been around for a long, long time. I've been on the scene a long, long time.
